messages.content: 一位化學家正在進行一個實驗，使用一個2公斤的特定物質A樣本。實驗開始時，該物質的初始溫度為攝氏25度。然後，化學家將物質加熱到最終溫度攝氏75度。該實驗在1大氣壓力下進行。化學家重複進行相同物質的實驗，但這次的初始溫度為攝氏10度，最終溫度為攝氏50度。你能計算出在這兩個實驗的設定初始和最終條件下，物質的熵變化嗎？

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

pressure.description: The pressure the substance is under in atmospheres.

message.content:
**Entropy change for a reversible heating process**

For a material heated reversibly from an initial temperature \(T_i\) to a final temperature \(T_f\) at constant pressure, the change in entropy is  

\[
\Delta S \;=\;\int_{T_i}^{T_f}\frac{dQ_{\text{rev}}}{T}
          \;=\;\int_{T_i}^{T_f}\frac{C_p\,dT}{T}
          \;=\;m\,C_p\,\ln\!\left(\frac{T_f}{T_i}\right)
\]

where  
\(m\) – mass of the sample (kg),  
\(C_p\) – specific heat capacity at constant pressure (J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹).

---

### Assumptions

Because the specific heat capacity of substance **A** was not supplied, we’ll use a typical value for many liquids/solids:

\[
C_p \approx 1.0 \times 10^3 \;\text{J kg}^{-1}\,\text{K}^{-1}
\]

(If you know the exact \(C_p\) for your material, simply replace this value.)

All temperatures are converted to Kelvin before applying the logarithm.

| Experiment | Initial \(T_i\) (°C) | Final \(T_f\) (°C) | \(T_i\) (K) | \(T_f\) (K) |
|------------|----------------------|--------------------|-------------|-------------|
| 1 | 25 | 75 | 298 | 348 |
| 2 | 10 | 50 | 283 | 323 |

---

### Calculations

#### 1. From 25 °C → 75 °C

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta S_1 &= m\,C_p\,\ln\!\left(\frac{T_f}{T_i}\right)\\[4pt]
           &= 2~\text{kg}\;\times\;1.0\times10^3~\frac{\text{J}}{\text{kg·K}}\;
              \times\;\ln\!\left(\frac{348}{298}\right)\\[4pt]
           &= 2000~\text{J K}^{-1}\;\times\;\ln(1.168)\\[4pt]
           &\approx 2000~\text{J K}^{-1}\;\times\;0.155\\[4pt]
           &\approx 3.1\times10^{2}\;\text{J K}^{-1}\\[4pt]
           &\boxed{3.1\times10^{2}\;\text{J K}^{-1}}
\end{aligned}
\]

#### 2. From 10 °C → 50 °C

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta S_2 &= 2~\text{kg}\;\times\;1.0\times10^3~\frac{\text{J}}{\text{kg·K}}\;
              \times\;\ln\!\left(\frac{323}{283}\right)\\[4pt]
           &= 2000~\text{J K}^{-1}\;\times\;\ln(1.141)\\[4pt]
           &\approx 2000~\text{J K}^{-1}\;\times\;0.132\\[4pt]
           &\approx 2.64\times10^{2}\;\text{J K}^{-1}\\[4pt]
           &\boxed{2.6\times10^{2}\;\text{J K}^{-1}}
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### Summary

| Experiment | Entropy change \(\Delta S\) |
|------------|---------------------------|
| 25 °C → 75 °C | \(3.1 \times 10^{2}\;\text{J K}^{-1}\) |
| 10 °C → 50 °C | \(2.6 \times 10^{2}\;\text{J K}^{-1}\) |

These values represent the increase in disorder (entropy) of the 2‑kg sample of substance **A** when heated reversibly under the stated conditions. If you have the precise specific heat capacity for your material, simply substitute that value into the formula above to obtain the exact numerical result.
